title: Heuristic kernel swaps: latency timeline & quant tradeoffs
body:
Purpose

Quick lab notebook describing a focused set of experiments to reproduce and characterize short-term latency spikes caused by heuristic kernel swaps when serving quantized models (INT8/AWQ, GPTQ variants, FP8). Goal is to produce deterministic repro steps, a timeline model for kernel swap events, and a set of mitigations we can trial in the runtime.

Background/context

We observed intermittent p95/p99 spikes on a handful of customer traces where the serving runtime switched kernel implementations mid-request. Spikes are especially visible for: long contexts (seq_len > 1024), mixed attention sparsity patterns, and request sequences that change tokenization/branching behavior mid-stream (e.g. code completion that flips from prose to code). Hypothesis: scheduler heuristics trigger a kernel switchover (tiling layout, vector-lane vs warps, or a numerics-safe fallback) which results in kernel reconfiguration, cache flushing, or small kernel launch contention — causing 10-80ms jitter on top of nominal generation latency.

Short summary of findings (top-level)

- Kernel-swap events correlate strongly with attention-window/profile changes and block-size mismatches between successive layers.
- AWQ-int8 variants show higher swap frequency when attention sparsity percentage crosses 18-22% (heuristic observed on A100 tests).
- FP8-backed kernels tend to keep steadier latency but have larger per-token time when batch sizes are small (1-2).
- Swap overhead is not purely kernel-launch time; we see a combination of: small reallocs in the KV cache, cuBLAS matmul reinitialization, and a short period where dispatcher queues small requests to a fallback execution lane.

Experiment matrix (what we ran)

Hardware: A100 80GB, H100 (dev farm).
Models: Llama-2-13B (reference checkpoint), mpt-7b-instruct (toy).
Quant configs: gptq-int8 (layerwise), awq-int8 (per-channel), fp8-e4m3-sim (experimental).
Kernels: default-block (our production), tiled-matmul-v2, vector-lane-optimized, warp-optimized, numerics-safe-fallback.
Workloads: single-request streaming chat (seq growth 64->1024), burst traffic (10 concurrent), synthetic attention-sparsity corpus (generated tokens with repeated long tokens and injected sparse attention mask).
Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency per token, end-to-end response, tokens/sec, kv-cache rebind count, kernel-switch-count (custom counter emitted by scheduler), device memcpy counts, CUDA kernel launch time distribution (from CUPTI traces), quality delta (perplexity change on heldout ml-qa set).

Representative command lines / harness

- bench harness (docker image): redwood/bench:v202604
- run: ./bench --model llama-13b --quant awq-int8 --kernel-policy heuristic --seq-profile long --trace cup-ti.out --out results/awq-llama-apr12
- trace extraction: python tools/cupti-parse.py results/awq-llama-apr12/cup-ti.out --emit-kernel-timeline > timeline.csv

Raw observations (selected)

1) Timeline example (single request, Llama-13b, A100, awq-int8):
- t=0ms request arrival
- t=12ms first tokens emitted (warm path)
- t=210ms tokenizer branch switch (prose->code) detected by runtime heuristics
- t=212ms kernel-swapping-start (dispatcher flagged tiled->vector-lane)
- t=219ms cuBLAS reinit / cublasLt plan update started
- t=235ms kernel-launches resume but with smaller occupancy (first block of new kernel stalls)
- t=260ms first token after swap
=> observable stall: ~50ms of additional latency around the swap.

2) Swap count vs sparsity (AWQ-int8, batch=1):
- sparsity < 10%: kernel-switch-count ~0 per 1k requests
- sparsity 15-20%: kernel-switch-count rises to 1.7 per 1k requests
- sparsity > 25%: kernel-switch-count spikes to 9 per 1k requests and p99 increases by 18%

3) FP8 variant: fewer switches (0.2 per 1k) but median token time +5ms compared to AWQ-int8 for batch=1. H100 shows similar trend but absolute times are ~20-30% lower.

Profiling evidence

- CUPTI traces show repeated small-kernel launches with different block shapes and shared-mem settings around the swap window.
- Flamegraphs show a clear gap where dispatcher code collects metrics and evaluates new kernel policy (cost function). That evaluation takes ~3-5ms and is synchronous in the current heuristic.
- KV-cache rebind events recorded in the trace coincide with kernel-swap-start in 78% of cases — indicates the cache shape/path is being reallocated when kernel changes.

Hypothesized root causes (ordered)

1) synchronous policy evaluation in dispatch path: runtime currently blocks to evaluate performance model before committing to a kernel variant. That evaluation was cheap in previous workloads but becomes visible for long sequential requests.
2) kernel code paths have mismatched memory layout expectations — swap triggers a tiny copy/repack of KV cache.
3) cuBLAS/cuDNN plan changes cause a micro-window during which launches queue up and the scheduler's small-launch fallback has lower occupancy.

Immediate mitigations we can try (cheap, trial quickly)

- Make heuristic evaluation async: allow running requests to continue on current kernel while spawning a background trial of new kernel on a small sample. If trial is faster, commit for subsequent tokens. This converts blocking cost into an amortized background cost.
- Debounce kernel-swap decisions: require metric delta > threshold for N tokens before committing swap.
- Preallocate KV-repack buffers for all allowed kernel layouts to avoid on-swap allocations. (Memory cost tradeoff).
- Add a short backoff window after a swap: do not consider further swaps for X tokens to avoid oscillation.

Longer-term engineering options

- Profile-guided static selection per model: build a tiny table mapping (sequence-length, sparsity, batch-size) -> kernel, computed offline by replay traces. Use that table as a fast index in runtime so we avoid runtime evaluation at the hot path.
- Incorporate a lightweight online estimator that samples a single micro-benchmark kernel invocation at low priority to keep policy updated without blocking.
- Kernel unification effort: reduce the number of sparse vs dense codegen forks; instead use a single flexible kernel that adapts tile size at runtime without requiring KV repack. (Harder).

Quality vs performance notes

- AWQ-int8 shows acceptable quality deltas on our small-qa test (perplexity delta < 3% relative) but the jitter risk may impact tail-SLA for interactive products.
- FP8 had slightly higher quality on some arithmetic-critical prompts (code-gen), but hardware availability and operator maturity are limiting.

Open questions / TODOs

- Can we reproduce the exact same swap behaviour on H100 with identical sequence? (Miguel to run A100->H100 parity test week of 2026-04-19).
- Measure memory vs latency trade for preallocating repack buffers across all kernel layouts (estimate memory cost for Llama-13b: ~4GB additional for 3 layouts).
- Add a counter into production debug logs for kernel-switch-count and kv-repack events (Riley owns INF-2413).
- Determine acceptable debounce thresholds: start with N=8 tokens or 50ms whichever comes first.

Notes-to-self / rough commands

- reproducer: tools/repro/run_kernel_swap_scenario.sh --model=llama-13b --quant=awq-int8 --inject-sparsity=20 --seq=1024 --out=swap-run-0408
- quick flame: ./scripts/flame.sh swap-run-0408/cupti.out > swap-run-0408/flame.svg

Decision points for PRs

- Small change: make heuristic eval async (low risk) -> PR: add background trial path (target: <2w).
- Medium: add debounce logic + fallback backoff (scheduler change, needs testing under multiworkload).
- Large: static offline policy table and prealloc plan (requires infra to collect traces and storage for tables).

Appendix: reproducible artifacts included

- results/awq-llama-apr12/timeline.csv (CUPTI-derived kernel timeline)
- results/awq-llama-apr12/kv-events.log
- bench config: bench/configs/llama-13b-awq-heuristic.yaml

If this matches what others have seen we should prioritize the async-eval + debounce experiment. Next meeting: sync with solutions-engineering to find a customer trace with repeatable repro (requested: Jun Park to pull candidate customer trace by 2026-04-21).

-- Asha
